channel.title: Islam Darawsheh Articles
channel.description: Practical articles on software architecture, enterprise .NET, secure systems, and maintainable software design.

item.title: MCP in .NET: What It Actually Solves and How to Build an MCP Server in C#
item.description: A practical .NET guide to Model Context Protocol: what MCP solves, how it differs from REST and function calling, and how to build a secure ASP.NET Core MCP server.

item.title: .NET 11: 9 New Features That Actually Matter to Developers
item.description: A practical look at nine .NET 11 features worth watching, from C# 15 unions and runtime async to HTTP request compression, ZIP encryption, EF Core vector search, Blazor, and .NET MAUI.

item.title: One Noisy Client Can Slow Everyone Down—Fix Your ASP.NET Core Rate Limiting
item.description: A production-minded ASP.NET Core 10 guide to rate-limit partitions, authenticated client identity, reverse proxies, endpoint cost, 429 responses, queueing, and multi-instance deployment trade-offs.

item.title: Your EF Core Pagination Is Slower Than You Think—Skip/Take Is Only Part of the Story
item.description: A practical .NET 10 and EF Core guide to choosing offset or keyset pagination based on UI requirements, total counts, deterministic ordering, indexes, and database-provider behavior.

item.title: Stop Exposing EF Core Entities from Your .NET 10 APIs
item.description: A production-minded .NET 10 guide to separating EF Core entities from HTTP API contracts using explicit request/response models, projections, TypedResults, and ProblemDetails.

item.title: Clean Architecture in .NET 10: Stop Adding Layers, Start Protecting Decisions
item.description: A production-minded .NET 10 walkthrough of Clean Architecture using UUIDv7, strong domain types, authoritative pricing, EF Core boundaries, Minimal APIs, and focused tests without unnecessary ceremony.

item.title: Clean Architecture vs. DDD Is Usually the Wrong Question
item.description: Clean Architecture and Domain-Driven Design are not competing alternatives. One governs dependency direction; the other helps teams model complex business domains.
